job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Young Rohan sat with his grandfather, listening to stories of the freedom struggle. Grandfather explained that the Indian National Congress, founded in 1885, was initially led by professionals like lawyers and teachers, not just poor farmers. He described how the British partitioned Bengal in 1905, claiming administrative ease, but the real goal was to divide the growing nationalist unity. When Rohan asked if Satyagraha meant being weak, his grandfather shook his head. He explained that Satyagraha was a powerful, active force of truth, not passive resistance. He then spoke of the 1930 Salt March. Gandhi chose salt because it was a basic necessity used by every household, regardless of wealth, making it a perfect symbol to challenge the British tax. Finally, they discussed the 1942 Quit India movement. Grandfather noted that while Gandhi advocated non-violence, the movement saw massive, spontaneous public participation that went far beyond just sitting quietly at home. He emphasized that the partition of India was a complex political outcome driven by specific leaders and policies, not an inevitable result of common people of different faiths being unable to live together in peace.

items.evidence: He described how the British partitioned Bengal in 1905, claiming administrative ease, but the real goal was to divide the growing nationalist unity.
items.q: The British said they split Bengal in 1905 for easier rule. What was their real aim?
options: To weaken the rising unity of nationalists
To make a very large province easier to run
To reward the lawyers and teachers of Congress
To stop Tilak's plans to use bombs
items.explain: Easier administration was only the claim; the real goal was to divide growing nationalist unity.

wrong.why: believes the stated reason of administrative ease
grabs a nearby detail about Congress leaders

items.evidence: He explained that Satyagraha was a powerful, active force of truth, not passive resistance.
items.q: How is Satyagraha different from simply staying quiet and doing nothing?
options: It is a strong, active stand for truth
It is a weak way of quietly giving in
It is the same as passive resistance
It is a violent force used against rulers
items.explain: Grandfather said Satyagraha is a powerful, active force of truth, not weakness or passive resistance.

wrong.why: misses the word 'not' before passive resistance
thinks a powerful force must be violent

items.evidence: Gandhi chose salt because it was a basic necessity used by every household, regardless of wealth, making it a perfect symbol to challenge the British tax.
items.q: Why did Gandhi pick salt to protest against British taxes in 1930?
options: Because every home, rich or poor, needed it
Because it was the costliest taxed luxury
Because only rich homes could afford it
Because only poor farmers' homes used it
items.explain: Salt was a basic need of every household, whatever its wealth, so it united everyone.

wrong.why: thinks salt was an expensive luxury
misreads 'regardless of wealth' as only the wealthy
over-generalises that the poor alone used salt

items.evidence: He emphasized that the partition of India was a complex political outcome driven by specific leaders and policies, not an inevitable result of common people of different faiths being unable to live together in peace.
items.q: Meena says Partition happened because ordinary Hindus and Muslims could not live together. How would Grandfather reply?
options: Certain leaders and policies mainly caused it
Hatred between common neighbours mainly caused it
Congress plans made in 1885 mainly caused it
British wish for easy administration mainly caused it
items.explain: Grandfather said Partition was a political outcome of specific leaders and policies, not ordinary people's hatred.

wrong.why: thinks common people's hatred caused Partition
thinks Pakistan was Congress's plan from the start
mixes up Partition with the Bengal partition reason
